messages.subject: model output not displaying estimates for all factor levels
parts:
I am currently working with the single season occu function. I have several covariates I am working with, and a number of them are factors with 2+ levels. here is a summary of my unmarkedframeoccu() model:

Site-level covariates:
          habitat             year          area              method                 Avg.snow       
Forest       : 72           2013: 90   Denali :173   track square: 39   Min.   :-1.84788  
Shrub        :165         2014:210   Susitna:127   transect    :261   1st Qu.:-0.81752  
Tundra Meadow: 63                                                                    Median :-0.06853  
                                                                                                    Mean   : 0.00000  
                                                                                                    3rd Qu.: 0.64420  
                                                                                                     Max.   : 3.57512  

Observation-level covariates:
      dist              dsls        
 Min.   :-1.8482   Min.   :-1.2580  
 1st Qu.:-0.8037   1st Qu.:-0.7925  
 Median : 0.1723   Median :-0.2815  
 Mean   : 0.0000   Mean   : 0.0000  
 3rd Qu.: 0.6226   3rd Qu.: 0.7455  
 Max.   : 4.5436   Max.   : 3.8267  
 NA's   :250       NA's   :250      

You can see my site level covariates are mostly factors. My question is this... when I run a model using any combination of factors to estimate p or psi the output does not show all factor levels. here is an example...

Call:
occu(formula = ~dist + method ~ habitat + snow, data = wt)

Occupancy:
                     Estimate    SE      z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)            -0.323 0.386 -0.838 0.40211
habitatShrub            0.531 0.467  1.137 0.25567
habitatTundra Meadow   -1.614 0.606 -2.662 0.00776
snow                   -0.481 0.233 -2.062 0.03922

Detection:
                Estimate    SE        z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)     0.000694 0.411  0.00169 9.99e-01
dist            0.749185 0.171  4.39131 1.13e-05
methodtransect -1.493691 0.464 -3.21773 1.29e-03

AIC: 565.3321 

This model estimates p as a function of dist (continuous) and method (factor), and psi as a function of snow (continuous) and habitat (factor). For both the factors the output lists the covariate name and then some, but not all, of the factor levels. For example, my habitat covariate has 3 levels (Forest, Shrub, TundraMeadow), but in the output I see "habitatshrub" and "habitattundrameadow" but no forest. When I use the predict() function I can get model predictions for all covariate levels, so I don't necessary think anything is wrong, I just don't understand why the output is displayed in this way. Any feedback would be appreciated. Thanks

Casey

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] model output not displaying estimates for all factor levels
parts:
hi Casey,
 when you have a factor level covariate , one of the levels has to be confounded with the intercept and so you would interpret the intercept as applying to that level. You can remove the intercept from the model with a "-1" in the model statement and all 3 factor levels should appear.
[note: this issue arises in every model fitting problem based on linear models]
regards
andy
